subject: P99 tailburst in v21-beta after Q8 rollout — emergency variant pin & SLA carveout request
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@grayline.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes after v21-beta Q8 rollout — need help

Hi Logan / team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency and a handful of 502s on our production traffic starting ~07:45 PDT after you rolled Q8 quantization to v21-beta. The average latency is okay but the tail is bursting — our users are reporting slow responses for contextual requests.

Attached: p99_tailburst-20260901.png and a tar with request-level logs (grayline_request_prod_logs.tar.gz).

Impact: ~1.7% of requests hit >2.5s p99 (previously ~0.9%), and we had ~40 502 errors in the last 30m. This is affecting a small subset of our power users but we need it addressed urgently.

Request: can you pin our traffic to v21-stable (pre-Q8) or enable an immediate fallback? We also need an ETA and whether this triggers an SLA exception.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform
GrayLine AI
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@grayline.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after v21-beta Q8 rollout — need help

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as an incident-level escalation.

Immediate asks:
- We can pin GrayLine's route to v21-stable (pre-Q8) within ~15m. That will stop the Q8 execution path for your traffic.
- We'd like to request a temporary SLA carveout for tail p99 while we do a fast investigation and either reconcile the Q8 kernels or roll the quantization back from the beta. Can you confirm you accept a 24–48 hour carveout window while we stabilise?

Priyom — can you confirm the quick mitigation plan (pin + investigate Q8 perf) and attach the analysis when ready.

Ben / Laura — need authorization to apply the pin and mark this as a provisional SLA exception for GrayLine pending postmortem. Ben — heads up to any commercial implications.

I'll start the pin as soon as I have confirmation.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@grayline.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after v21-beta Q8 rollout — need help

On Tue, Sep 1, 2026 at 09:05 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Priyom — can you confirm the quick mitigation plan (pin + investigate Q8 perf) and attach the analysis when ready.

Quick summary from the initial investigation (attached v21-beta-q8-analysis.pdf):
- Root cause hypothesis: new Q8 kernels for v21-beta increase attention kernel spillover on longer-context requests and interact poorly with KV-cache reuse patterns for some prompt shapes. This increases CPU/GPU sync waits causing tail latency to spike.
- Repro: we reproduced p99 delta locally with a subset of GrayLine request traces in a canary harness when Q8 enabled.
- Short-term options: 1) Pin GrayLine to v21-stable (pre-Q8) — fastest and low-risk. 2) Enable automatic variant fallback when latency >1.5s for a rolling window (requires config change, ~30–45m). 3) Roll back Q8 globally for v21-beta (higher blast radius).

I'll attach the detailed perf diff and kernel flame graphs (see v21-beta-q8-analysis.pdf). My recommendation: pin for now + enable automatic fallback for 2–4 hours while we patch the Q8 kernel selection logic.

If we pin, we'll need ops approval for a provisional SLA carveout while the client experiences degraded p99 before we've fully mitigated.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Backend Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachments: v21-beta-q8-analysis.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@grayline.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after v21-beta Q8 rollout — need help

Thanks team. Ben here — looping in commercial context for GrayLine (deal GL-4582).

From a customer success / commercial perspective: pinning to v21-stable and a short SLA carveout is acceptable. GrayLine is sensitive to any user-visible regressions; we should prioritize avoiding user-facing errors.

Two asks from my side:
1) Approve provisional carveout for up to 48 hours while we investigate — we should aim to close sooner.
2) If we do a pin, we should offer GrayLine a small goodwill credit if the carveout exceeds 24 hours; Laura, can you confirm we have credit authority or if we need legal/finance sign-off?

Samir — we'll proceed with the pin and fallback plan once ops authorizes; Ben will coordinate any commercial note for the account.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@grayline.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Authorization: emergency pin + provisional SLA carveout (GrayLine)

I've reviewed the context and Priyom's analysis. Authorization:
- Ops authorizes pinning GrayLine traffic to v21-stable immediately. Logan, apply the change and monitor traffic for the next 2 hours.
- Provisional SLA carveout approved for up to 48 hours while we perform the kernel fix and full validation. Please document the carveout in INF-4523 and create a postmortem within 72 hours.
- Ben: you have provisional approval to promise a goodwill credit only if the carveout exceeds 24 hours; legal/finance should not be looped unless we exceed that duration.

Samir — we'll apply the pin now and follow up with a short status update in 30–60m. Sorry for the disruption; appreciate the fast report and logs.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
